cohort: 399 women, including 197 non-pregnant women, 168 nulliparous pregnant women, and 124 multiparous women
finding: The study found that perfectionism and intolerance of uncertainty were the most important determinants of fear of childbirth in non-pregnant and nulliparous pregnant women, while previous experience of emergency cesarean section was the most important determinant in multiparous women.
mod_finding: Previous experience of emergency cesarean section was associated with increased fear of childbirth in multiparous women.
